text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing how it works. The main goal is to make the code cleaner and easier to understand, not to add new features. For example, you might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller ones, or simplify complicated logic. By doing this, you reduce technical debt—the extra work caused by rushing and writing messy code. Clearer code is also much easier for other developers to read and maintain. While refactoring takes time, it saves hours later and helps prevent bugs. Think of it as tidying your desk before starting a big project.
